pages.text: "No! I won't sleep!" Upstairs, little brother Mumu played a straw flute. Peep, peep! Stars filled the night beyond the round window; a little lamp stood by his pillow. Mumu held back a yawn. "Just a little more, a little more!"
Dad from the mill came in. "Mumu, I'm closing the sluice gate, the door that holds back stream water. When it closes, it's bedtime." "I'm not sleepy at all!" Mumu shook his head and hugged the flute.
But his beak opened wide all by itself. Yaaawn! The flute dropped from his wing. His eyes were half closed. "Oh? Maybe I'm a little sleepy...?"
Dad held Mumu in both wings by the stream's sluice gate. The wheel was still splashing round. "Let's close it together." Dad set Mumu's wing on the handle.

With wings together, they lowered the gate. Creeeak! The water stopped, and the wheel slowly... slowly... stood still. Only the stream trickled. "Wow. Quiet." Mumu stayed still with his beak a little open.
Dad whispered beside Mumu's head. "See? When the wheel stops, the whole mill sleeps." At the upstairs round window, big sister Dodo yawned too. Mumu repeated, "Waterwheel stops—sleep tight!"
Back upstairs, Mumu slipped under the covers. Dad bent low, touched his beak tip to Mumu's forehead, and hummed softly, "Waterwheel stops—sleep tight!"

The little lamp was blown out. The room was dark, with only the stream trickling. Mumu looked at the flute and whispered, "Sleep tight, flute." Under the covers, one flick of his tail, then eyes closed.
Now Mumu knew bedtime. "One, gate closed, flute rests too! Two, under the covers! Three, lamp out, sleep tight!" Under the next covers, Dodo was already breathing softly.
Morning came. The wheel splashed round again, and the room was bright. Dad hugged Mumu in both wings. "After a good sleep, morning feels lively, right?" Mumu smiled. "Waterwheel stops—sleep tight!"
